clue.text: Censor performance by cardinal

blocks.note: cardinal is a deep red colour, from the robes of cardinals
an act is a turn or performance on stage

explanation.surface: A church cardinal's staged show gets cut by the censor.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads in reverse clue order: the cardinal's colour comes first, then the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact a document is to black out sensitive passages before release, which is what a censor does.

clue.text: Actual banks went for compensation

indicators.note: banks line a river on both sides, so one word flanks the other

blocks.note: real means actual, genuine
to quit is to leave, so went is quit

explanation.surface: Financial banks paid out real money in compensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' sounds like the financial institutions; it is a verb, edging the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: Requital is repayment or return for a loss, service or injury, the same as recompense.

clue.text: King invested in vacuous plan

indicators.note: money invested in a business is put inside it, so the royal letter goes within

blocks.note: daft means silly, empty-headed
R for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch puts money into a foolish scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or sketch of a document, an outline scheme.

clue.text: Brew cups instead for team

indicators.note: to cup something is to hold it in curved hands, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: cha is British slang for tea
else means otherwise, instead

explanation.surface: Tea served in cups for a sports team after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cups' looks like teacups or football trophies; it is the verb. CHELSEA is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea FC is a Premier League football club based in west London, so it is a sports team.

clue.text: Something like a tablet best served with drink

blocks.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does, with the tongue
top means best, as in top quality

explanation.surface: Sounds like a pill best taken with a drink, as a doctor might advise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablet' suggests medicine taken with water; here it is the computer kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable computer is a close relative of a tablet device, both being small personal computing machines.

clue.text: Hostile to Gaul, oddly, a Caribbean island

indicators.note: oddly points to the letters in odd-numbered positions of the word it follows

blocks.note: anti means against or opposed to
first and third letters of the ancient name for France
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resentful towards the French heads for a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is the larger island of Antigua and Barbuda, a nation in the eastern West Indies.

clue.text: Calculator provided when Aristotle messed up!

indicators.note: something messed up is in disarray, so the philosopher's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Greek philosopher's name, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A great thinker's error forced the use of a calculating machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A totaliser is a device that adds up amounts, such as betting stakes at a racecourse, so it computes.

clue.text: Cheer penny put on rent

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
to lease property is to rent it

explanation.surface: A tenant is delighted to have a penny added to the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'put on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to gladden or delight them, raising their spirits.

clue.text: Confront attacker, dinosaur winning!

definitions.note: the definition includes its object: one squares up to an attacker

blocks.note: a dinosaur is an old-fashioned person, someone unfashionably conventional
a side that is up is ahead or winning

explanation.surface: Someone faces down an assailant while a dinosaur comes out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: The dinosaur is not a prehistoric reptile but a fogey, someone stuck in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To square up to someone is to adopt a fighting stance, ready to face an opponent physically.

clue.text: Isn't prickle irritating in tight garment!

indicators.note: irritating suggests agitation and chafing, so these letters are stirred into new order

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A wearer insists a figure-hugging garment does not itch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil skirt is a slim, straight, close-fitting skirt, typically falling to the knee.

clue.text: Appear shaky in summer?

blocks.note: first meaning: to walk unsteadily, wobbling
second meaning: one who sums, an adder-up of figures

explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' looks like the season, but read it as sum-mer, a person who adds things up; the question mark flags the coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to wobble unsteadily, and as a noun it is one who tots or totals numbers.

clue.text: Sweet William in two beds

indicators.note: a bed holds something within it, so the following words harbour the letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the name and the next two words

explanation.surface: A gardener plants sweet williams in two flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet William' is a familiar garden flower, so the phrase begs to be read together; split it after 'Sweet'. MINT lies inside williaM IN Two.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint is a peppermint-flavoured confection, a common kind of boiled or chocolate candy.

clue.text: African seen in a tizzy after drinking, for instance, pub offerings

indicators.note: a tizzy is a state of flustered agitation, so these letters are thrown into disorder
drinking means taking something in, so the scrambled word swallows what follows

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
e.g. is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
beers served at a pub

explanation.surface: An African visitor gets flustered after a few pints at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinking' suggests booze to match the pub, but here it means taking in: the jumbled word holds the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A Senegalese person comes from Senegal, a country in West Africa, so is an African.

clue.text: Wild things, Con-dor and Lab-rador, might you say?

blocks.note: surface reading: wild creatures such as a bird of prey and a dog breed
setter's reading: each beast's name starts with a British political party, Con(servative) and Lab(our)

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphens split each animal so that it begins with a party name: Con for Conservative, Lab for Labour, Britain's two main parties.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is idiom for wild revellers who love going out to celebrations, punningly also creatures named after political groups.

clue.text: Listed row covering deck awfully old

indicators.note: a covering goes around something, so the quarrel wraps the rest
awfully means badly, so the playing-surface word is badly jumbled

blocks.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel, a row
taken as written, to be jumbled
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A row on a ship's deck goes horribly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listed' suggests a ship leaning over, fitting the deck and row; it means entered and checked on a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Items ticked off a list have been checked and recorded one by one, so they are listed.

clue.text: Mushroom cocktail!

blocks.note: first meaning: to grow rapidly, as a verb
second meaning: a drink of advocaat and lemonade

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushroom' looks like the fungus, but it is the verb for swelling fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to grow increasingly fast, like a rolling ball of packed ice, and the noun names an advocaat drink.

clue.text: Mean task at the deli counter?

blocks.note: first meaning: stingy, penny-pinching
second meaning, read literally: slicing the rind off a block of dairy produce

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second meaning as a literal, playful reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy economy over trifles is the idiomatic sense, from shaving rind thin so nothing is wasted.

clue.text: Draconian measures originally cutting old oak, say?

indicators.note: originally points to the start, the opening letter of the word
something cutting into a word splits it, sitting inside it

blocks.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
an oak is an example of one, signalled by say
opening letter of measures

explanation.surface: Harsh measures began with felling an ancient oak.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian laws are excessively harsh, the most severe possible, so they go to an extreme.

clue.text: Game taking place also in outskirts of Preston

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the outer letters are used
in places the other pieces inside the edges of the town

blocks.note: first and last letters of the Lancashire town
an event that is on is happening
too means also

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture happens on the edge of Preston, a town in Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontoon is a card game, the British name for twenty-one or blackjack.

clue.text: License what one might do with straight hair?

definitions.text: what one might do with straight hair?

blocks.note: first meaning: to allow or authorise, a verb

blocks.clueFragment: what one might do with straight hair?
blocks.note: second meaning, split in two: give the hair a curling treatment

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags splitting the word into PERM IT: a perm is a chemical curling treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit is to allow or authorise something formally, the verb sense of license.

clue.text: Tedious, might one be rambling?

blocks.note: first meaning: dull, uninspired
second meaning: a person going on foot, as a rambler or hiker does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' suggests talking at boring length, tying it to the first meaning; here it is walking.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means dull and plodding, and the noun is someone travelling on foot rather than by vehicle.

clue.text: One unseen with hand in puppet

indicators.note: something unseen is absent from view, so the numeral for one must go missing

blocks.note: a paw is informal for a hand
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one, which is then removed

explanation.surface: A glove puppet works with a hand in it, the puppeteer unseen.
explanation.walkthrough: PAW + IN gives PAWIN; taking out the I (one) leaves PAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn is a person used and manipulated by others, just as a puppet is controlled.

clue.text: Particular sink at home's blocked

indicators.note: a blocked pipe has something stuck inside it, so one word lodges within

blocks.note: to pot a ball in snooker is to sink it
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A household sink gets blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' looks like the kitchen kind; it is the verb, as in potting a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A point is an individual detail or item in an argument, and particulars are such details.

clue.text: Force confession from model, enthralling maiden

indicators.note: to enthrall is to hold captive, so one piece holds the other inside it

blocks.note: a model might confess what they do: I pose
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A model is made to own up, while a young woman looks on captivated.
explanation.walkthrough: The model's words 'I pose' wrap around M to give I-M-POSE. A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose something is to force it upon others, laying it on them without consent.

clue.text: Hot apricot in a stew gets left

indicators.note: a stew is a jumbled mixture cooked together, so the fruit's letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A hot fruit stew is served with the apricot left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical regions near the equator are hot and humid, so the word is used loosely for sweltering weather.

clue.text: Peg fed rotten sweet

indicators.note: something fed takes food in, so the first word receives the other inside it

blocks.note: a tee is the little peg a golf ball sits on
food that has gone off is rotten

explanation.surface: Someone named Peg was given spoilt food.
explanation.walkthrough: Peg looks like a woman's name, but it is the little golf peg the ball sits on before a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection made by boiling sugar with butter, a classic British candy.

clue.text: A-list jerks embracing new fix

indicators.note: jerks are sudden jolting movements that shake these letters out of order
to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the jumbled letters wrap round another

blocks.note: the hyphenated phrase taken letter for letter, to be jumbled
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Celebrity idiots fawn over a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerks' looks like a noun for fools but works as a verb. INSTAL is a less common spelling of install.
explanation.definitionFit: To instal equipment is to put it in place and secure it, which is to fix it.
